Alexandre Dumas, The Black Tulip, translated by P. F. Collier and Son.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/alexandre-dumas/the-black-tulip/p-f-collier-and-son

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Alexandre Dumas, the author, died 1870 (citizenship: France).
- P. F. Collier and Son, the translator, died 1909 (a publishing firm, listed with the death year recorded for Wikidata Q7173900) (citizenship: United States).

First publication of the text used: 1902 (SE colophon: 'The Black Tulip was published in 1850 by Alexandre Dumas. It was translated from French in 1902 by P. F. Collier and Son.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1902, before 1931. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 1997.
- Country of origin (the country of first publication is not named in the facts): the work is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last person to die did so in 1909.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
